_about: The kinds of video MAGI can make. Each type is a template the video agents follow: its beats (the engine's five-beat, 30-second scene), the kind of hook, the camera, on-screen text, voice and the references it needs. The Strategist suggests a type for every video idea and says why; the idea card lets you change it. Types with "generate": false need real footage (people, customers, the factory) and are never made with AI, so no real person or customer is faked. Reach notes are estimates from marketing write-ups, not measured on MAGPPIE's own posts; tune them against your own results.

types.label: Story / mini-drama
types.best_for: Emotion and brand memory: a small moment in a family's day where the kitchen quietly makes life easier.
types.reach: high for shares and follows when the moment feels true (estimate)
types.hook: Open on a person in the middle of a relatable moment, never on the product. The first line names a feeling or a small problem.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: a person mid-moment in the kitchen, a small tension or wish
0:05-0:12 the moment unfolds: the everyday task, the kitchen in use
0:12-0:20 the turn: the stone does what it promises, shown not told
0:20-0:27 the payoff: relief, a smile, the family together
0:27-0:30 exit frame on the kitchen at rest; the line that lands the idea
types.camera: Handheld-feeling but steady, eye level, close and medium shots, natural window light, one continuous home.
types.on_screen_text: None, or one short line at the end.
types.voice: A warm first-person or close narrator, conversational, one breath per line.
types.people: One or two people, faces turned away or out of focus (no close-up faces).
types.cautions: No health claims. The product is the quiet hero, never a lecture.

types.label: Before and after
types.best_for: Stopping the scroll and reaching new viewers: a tired kitchen becomes a SILVERSTONE kitchen.
types.reach: among the highest for new viewers in home and interior content (estimate)
types.hook: Show the 'before' problem in the first second: swollen doors, a damp corner, a cabinet that no longer closes. Never name another brand.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the before, a worn or damp kitchen, the problem visible
0:05-0:12 closer on what goes wrong over the years
0:12-0:20 the reveal: the same space as a SILVERSTONE kitchen
0:20-0:27 details of the after: surfaces, doors, light
0:27-0:30 exit frame on the finished kitchen; the line that lands the change
types.camera: Matched framing between before and after (same angle, same lens) so the change reads instantly; a slow push on the reveal.
types.on_screen_text: Two words at most: BEFORE, then AFTER, or none.
types.voice: Calm and confident; let the reveal breathe without speech for a second.
types.cautions: The 'before' is a generic tired kitchen, never a named brand or a competitor's product. Nothing 'kills' pests: they find nothing to eat.

types.label: Demonstration / proof
types.best_for: Proving one claim the viewer can see: water on a seam, a stain wiped away, a door that stays true.
types.hook: Start the test in the first second: 'Pour it on the seam. Wait an hour.'
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the test begins, close on the stone
0:05-0:12 the test runs: time passes, the camera stays on it
0:12-0:20 the result, shown up close
0:20-0:27 why it holds: the material, in one plain line
0:27-0:30 exit frame on the clean surface; the line that lands the proof
types.camera: Macro and close shots, locked-off or slow slide, raking light that shows texture.
types.on_screen_text: A short time stamp ('1 hour later') or none.
types.voice: Matter of fact, short sentences, no hype.
types.cautions: Only claims in the approved claims and company knowledge. No 'antibacterial', no percentages, no health claims.

types.label: Reveal
types.best_for: Curiosity: hidden storage, drawers, an appliance garage, a kitchen shown piece by piece.
types.hook: Tease what is hidden: a closed wall of stone, a hand reaching for it.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: a closed, calm surface; something is behind it
0:05-0:12 the first opening: a drawer or door slides open
0:12-0:20 more is revealed, one piece at a time
0:20-0:27 the whole kitchen, everything in its place
0:27-0:30 exit frame closing again, silent and tidy
types.camera: Slow, smooth moves, push-ins on each opening, soft even light.
types.on_screen_text: None, or a one-word label per reveal.
types.voice: Quiet, almost a whisper at the start, growing a little at the end.
types.cautions: Show only fittings MAGPPIE really makes.

types.label: Problem, process, outcome
types.best_for: Explaining one benefit clearly: the problem a viewer has, how MAGPPIE solves it, the result.
types.reach: steady, good for saves and enquiries (estimate)
types.hook: Name the viewer's problem in their own words in the first line.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the problem, plainly
0:05-0:12 why it happens
0:12-0:20 how a SILVERSTONE kitchen avoids it
0:20-0:27 the outcome in daily life
0:27-0:30 exit frame; the line that lands the benefit
types.camera: Clean medium and close shots, calm pacing, consistent light.
types.on_screen_text: Up to three short labels, one per stage, or none.
types.voice: Clear and friendly, like explaining to a neighbour.
types.people: Optional; hands or a figure at a distance.
types.cautions: No health claims; pests find nothing to eat, nothing is killed.

types.label: POV / day in the life
types.best_for: Relatable first-person moments: a morning, a monsoon week, ten years on.
types.reach: high for shares when the moment is familiar (estimate)
types.hook: 'POV: ...' as the first line, a moment the viewer recognises.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the POV line, seen through the viewer's eyes
0:05-0:12 the routine begins in the kitchen
0:12-0:20 the moment that would go wrong in an ordinary kitchen does not
0:20-0:27 the calm that follows
0:27-0:30 exit frame; a short closing line
types.camera: First-person angle, hands in frame, natural light changing with the time of day.
types.on_screen_text: The POV line at the top for the first beat.
types.cautions: Keep it everyday; no exaggerated claims.

types.label: Tips list
types.best_for: Saves and shares: 'three things that ruin a kitchen', 'what to check before you buy'.
types.hook: Promise a number in the first line: 'Three things that quietly ruin a kitchen.'
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the promise and the number
0:05-0:12 tip one, shown
0:12-0:20 tip two, shown
0:20-0:27 tip three, where SILVERSTONE comes in
0:27-0:30 exit frame; 'save this for later'
types.camera: One clear shot per tip, quick but not rushed cuts on the beat.
types.on_screen_text: A number and two or three words per tip (1, 2, 3).
types.voice: Brisk and helpful, one tip per breath.
types.cautions: Tips must be true to company knowledge; no competitor named.

types.label: Myth vs fact / common mistakes
types.best_for: Comments and debate: a common belief about kitchens, and what is true.
types.hook: State the myth as if true, then stop on it: 'Stone kitchens are cold and hard to live with.'
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: the myth, stated
0:05-0:12 why people believe it
0:12-0:20 the fact, shown
0:20-0:27 what that means at home
0:27-0:30 exit frame; ask the viewer what they believed
types.camera: Two looks: the myth slightly cooler, the fact warm and clear.
types.voice: Light, a little playful, never smug.
types.people: Optional; hands or a figure at a distance.
types.cautions: Never name or mock another brand; facts only from company knowledge.

types.label: Material story
types.best_for: Explaining SILVERSTONE itself: stone with silver and copper, and why it matters.
types.hook: Start on the material: 'Stone, silver, copper. Three materials, and no wood.'
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: extreme close-up of the stone
0:05-0:12 what it is made of, shown as texture and light
0:12-0:20 from slab to kitchen
0:20-0:27 the kitchen in daily use
0:27-0:30 exit frame; the line that lands what the material means
types.camera: Macro texture shots moving out to the full kitchen, slow and precise.
types.voice: Measured and confident, a touch of wonder.
types.cautions: Only what the knowledge says about the material; never name a stone colour in the voice-over.

types.label: Finish showcase
types.best_for: Showing the range: several finishes in quick, beautiful cuts.
types.hook: A striking finish fills the frame in the first second, no words needed.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: one finish fills the frame
0:05-0:12 two more finishes, each in a kitchen
0:12-0:20 two more, different rooms or light
0:20-0:27 the range side by side
0:27-0:30 exit frame; invite the viewer to pick a favourite
types.camera: Clean, matched framing per finish, cuts on the music beat.
types.on_screen_text: None (finish names are not spoken; they may appear as small labels in the edit).
types.voice: Very little: one line at the start and one at the end.
types.cautions: Use only real finish swatches; never name a colour or finish in the voice-over.

types.label: Sensory / ASMR
types.best_for: Calm, satisfying watching: the sound of a drawer closing, stone wiped clean.
types.hook: A close, satisfying sound and texture in the first second.
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: a close sound and texture
0:05-0:12 a second satisfying action
0:12-0:20 a third, building calm
0:20-0:27 the whole kitchen, quiet
0:27-0:30 exit frame; one short spoken line or silence
types.camera: Macro, very slow, soft light, nothing hurried.
types.voice: Almost none: at most one short line at the end; the sound carries the film.
types.cautions: Keep it calm; no claims needed.

types.label: Side by side
types.best_for: A clear comparison: a wooden kitchen and a stone kitchen through the same years.
types.hook: Two kitchens, one frame: 'Same kitchen. Ten monsoons later.'
beats: 0:00-0:05 hook: split frame, both kitchens new
0:05-0:12 time passes on both sides
0:12-0:20 the wooden side shows wear; the stone side does not
0:20-0:27 close on the difference
0:27-0:30 exit frame on the stone kitchen; the line that lands it
types.camera: Split screen or matched cuts with identical framing.
types.on_screen_text: Labels such as WOOD and STONE, or a year count.
types.cautions: Wood in general, never a named brand or competitor. Nothing 'kills' pests.

types.label: Talking head / expert
types.best_for: Trust and personality: a designer or expert explains one idea to camera.
types.reach: high when the person is natural and unpolished (estimate)
types.hook: The first sentence is the answer, not the introduction.
types.camera: Needs your own footage of a real person.
types.people: A real person, filmed with consent.

types.label: Customer story
types.best_for: Proof from a real home: a customer and their kitchen.
types.hook: The customer's own line about what changed.
types.camera: Needs your own footage of a real customer and home.
types.on_screen_text: Captions and the customer's first name, with consent.
types.people: A real customer, filmed with consent.
types.cautions: Never generated with AI; no invented reviews.

types.label: Behind the scenes
types.best_for: Craft and trust: the factory, the install, the team at work.
types.hook: Start mid-process on something the viewer has never seen.
types.camera: Needs your own footage from the factory or a site.
types.voice: A team member or a narrator.

types.label: Founder story
types.best_for: The why behind MAGPPIE, in the founders' own words.
types.hook: One honest sentence about why the company exists.
types.camera: Needs your own footage of the founders.
types.cautions: Never generated with AI. The family names are Subah and Ishat.

types.label: Trend reaction
types.best_for: Joining a conversation: a kitchen trend, and MAGPPIE's honest take.
types.reach: high while the trend is live (estimate)
types.hook: Show the trend first, then the reaction.
types.camera: Needs your own footage of a presenter reacting.
types.cautions: Never generated with AI; never mock another brand.
